--- title: "Nepal Electoral Constituency GeoJSON" description: "Scraping a constituency map from an election results site, converting its SVG paths to GIS geometry, and georeferencing it against ward boundaries in R." image-alt: "Map of Nepal's electoral constituencies in grey with national parks highlighted in green." subtitle: "Scraping SVG, converting to GIS, and Georeferencing data with R" author: - name: Pukar Bhandari email: pukar.bhandari@outlook.com image: "nepal_election_geojson.png" date: "2026-01-18" categories: [R, GIS, Data Science] prefer-html: true resources: - "output/*.geojson" - "output/*.svg" code-links: - text: Source of this post icon: github href: https://github.com/ar-puuk/ar-puuk.github.io/blob/master/posts/nepal-election-geojson/index.qmd --- ## Introduction In this workflow, we tackle a common geospatial problem: extracting data from stylized news graphics (like election heatmaps) and converting them into GIS-ready formats. Rather than just cleaning the rough edges of a scraped SVG, we will use a **reconstruction technique**. We will: 1. **Scrape** the electoral map to get rough constituency shapes (@sec-scrape, @sec-parse). 2. **Georeference** the shapes to align them with real coordinates (@sec-georef). 3. **Reconstruct** the precise boundaries by grouping official administrative "Wards" based on which constituency shape they fall into (@sec-wards). ::: {.content-visible when-format="html"} ```{mermaid} %%| label: fig-workflow %%| fig-cap: "The workflow: rough shapes from the scraped map, precise boundaries from the wards." flowchart LR A["Scrape
SVG"] --> B["Parse and
georeference"] B --> C["Rough
shapes"] W["Official
wards"] --> D["Match each ward
to a shape"] C --> D D --> E["Dissolve by
constituency"] E --> F["Final
GeoJSON"] ``` ::: ::: {.column-margin} The constituency map comes from the [2079 general election heatmap](https://generalelection2079.ekantipur.com/heatmap) on ekantipur. Ward boundaries are the official administrative layer saved in this post's `data/` folder. ::: ## Setup and Libraries We use `sf` for spatial operations and `rvest` for scraping. We also define paths for our inputs (official ward data) and outputs. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Show the setup code"} library(sf) # Spatial data handling library(xml2) # Parsing XML/SVG library(rvest) # Web scraping library(httr2) # HTTP requests library(stringr) # String manipulation library(dplyr) # Data manipulation library(here) # Robust project-relative paths post_dir <- here("posts", "nepal-election-geojson") # <1> wards_geojson_path <- here::here(post_dir, "data", "nepal-wards.gpkg") # <2> national_geojson_path <- here::here(post_dir, "data", "nepal-national.gpkg") output_svg_path <- here::here(post_dir, "output", "nepal_electoral_map.svg") # <3> rough_map_path <- here::here(post_dir, "output", "nepal_svg_rough.geojson") output_geojson_path <- here::here(post_dir, "output", "nepal_electoral_map.geojson") if (!dir.exists(dirname(output_svg_path))) dir.create(dirname(output_svg_path), recursive = TRUE) # <4> ``` ::: 1. The path to this post's own folder, so the code runs from anywhere in the project. 2. Official ward and national boundaries, used as the reference. 3. Where the three outputs are written. 4. Create the output folder if it is missing. ## Scraping the SVG {#sec-scrape} We use `httr2` to fetch the webpage and `rvest` to extract the specific SVG element containing the map. We also inject some CSS to ensure the map renders correctly if viewed in a browser (e.g., setting the viewBox and handling overflow). ::: {.callout-warning} ## The source site is not under your control The code sends a browser-like user agent, because the site can refuse bare requests, and it falls back to the SVG saved by an earlier run if the site is down. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} url <- "https://generalelection2079.ekantipur.com/heatmap" message("Fetching data from: ", url) tryCatch({ req <- request(url) |> req_user_agent("Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36") # <1> resp <- req_perform(req) html_content <- resp_body_html(resp) svg_node <- html_element(html_content, xpath = "//svg[.//pattern[@id='np__BG']]") # <2> if (!inherits(svg_node, "xml_missing")) { xml_set_attr(svg_node, "viewBox", "0 0 1920 1080") # <3> css_styles <- " path { fill: #cccccc; stroke: #fff; cursor: pointer; stroke-width: 1.75px; } path:hover { opacity: 0.9; } .national-park { fill: #55e5a5 !important; } svg { overflow: visible !important; } " xml_add_child(svg_node, "style", css_styles, .where = 0) # <4> write_xml(svg_node, output_svg_path) message("Success! Raw SVG saved to: ", output_svg_path) } else { warning("SVG element not found on the page.") } }, error = function(e) { message("Error fetching URL: ", e$message) }) if (!exists("svg_node") && file.exists(output_svg_path)) { # <5> message("Using the previously saved SVG: ", output_svg_path) svg_node <- read_xml(output_svg_path) } ``` ::: 1.
